title: Darwin's Game
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: High schooler Kaname Sudo accepts an invite to a phone game and finds himself in a real-life fight to the death where every player gets a superpower called a Sigil. He survives by wits, forms a clan with the 'Undefeated Queen' Shuka and others, and fights yakuza-run clans while hunting for the Game Master. Later arcs reveal the game trains champions against monsters that replace people across worlds.
life_message: It holds up loyalty to your own clan and refusing to kill when you can, inside a world that rewards killing.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Clans have leaders and ranks set by strength and points.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Strategy and calculation, not custom, decide survival.

folkways.japan: Yakuza clans, Shibuya turf and a reluctant ordinary student hero reflect Japanese crime-fiction and death-game genre conventions.

winners_losers: Kaname's clan and those who keep some restraint win; sadists like Wang lose. Sympathy goes to loyal, strategic survivors.
